metaDescription: Eluo (also Alluolue) is the yam festival of the chiefs and people of Sefwi Wiawso in the Western North Region: a week of events ending in a grand durbar.
subtitle: The Sefwi yam festival
answer: Eluo, also written Alluolue or Elluo, is the yam festival of the chiefs and people of the Sefwi Wiawso Traditional Area in the Western North Region. It runs for about a week and ends with a grand durbar of chiefs at Sefwi Wiawso, the regional capital. The Wiawso Traditional Council sets the dates each year; in 2023 it was held from October into mid-November.

sections.title: What happens
sections.html:
Eluo is a yam festival, kept by the chiefs and people of Sefwi Wiawso and, by some accounts, Sefwi Bekwai.[[4]] The traditional council describes it as a time for unity and for taking stock of the year.[[1]]

The 2023 festival ran for a week of events: a drumming and dancing competition, a candlelight procession, a quiz between districts, a football gala, a health walk with screening, Mr and Miss Eluo, and a cooking competition.[[1]] It ended with a grand durbar in Sefwi Wiawso, hosted by the Omanhene of Sefwi Wiawso, with paramount chiefs from other traditional areas as guests.[[2]]

In 2023 the council banned funerals in the traditional area from 19 October, and lifted the ban when the festival ended on 16 November.[[3]]

Other Sefwi towns keep the festival too. At Sefwi Akontombra it is a thanksgiving to the ancestors for seeing the chiefs and people through the year without serious calamity.[[5]]

sections.title: When is Eluo?
sections.html: There is no fixed date. Older accounts put Eluo in July, others in November or December.[[4]] In 2023 the council launched the festival in August for October, and it closed on 16 November.[[1,3]] Look out for the council’s launch, usually a couple of months ahead.

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Sefwi Wiawso is the capital of the Western North Region. See the Western North page for places nearby.
Funerals: in 2023 they were banned during the festival. If you are in the area for one, check with the family first.
Check the dates: the traditional council announces them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the launch.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.

faq.a: The yam festival of the chiefs and people of the Sefwi Wiawso Traditional Area in the Western North Region, ending with a grand durbar of chiefs.
The traditional council sets the dates each year. In 2023 it ran from October to 16 November.
